title: Eli Lilly to acquire Calytrix Bio in US$1.5B deal for blood cancer antibody | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication

contentHtml:
USA—Eli Lilly has agreed to acquire Massachusetts-based Calytrix Bio for up to US$1.5 billion to expand its oncology pipeline, adding an investigational antibody targeting mutant calreticulin-driven essential thrombocythemia (ET) and myelofibrosis (MF).

Under the definitive agreement, Calytrix Bio shareholders will receive an upfront cash payment, followed by additional payments tied to the achievement of specified clinical and regulatory milestones.

The structure links part of the acquisition value to the candidate’s progress through development and potential regulatory approval.

Targeted antibody approach

The investigational biparatopic antibody is designed to target both Type 1 and Type 2 mutant calreticulin (mCALR), proteins expressed on the surface of affected tumour cells.

Its mechanism is intended to eliminate disease-driving mutant cells while sparing healthy tissues and preserving normal blood cell production.

The candidate is also being developed with a safety and administration profile intended to support its use as an initial treatment and for extended therapy.

This approach addresses an unmet need in the management of myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), a group of blood cancers associated with abnormal production of blood cells.

By targeting the genetic mutations responsible for disease progression, the programme aims to move beyond treatments that primarily control symptoms and complications.

Its development could broaden the range of targeted treatment approaches for patients with mCALR-driven ET and MF.

Calytrix Bio President and CEO Brad Prosek said the company was established on the belief that patients with MPNs need treatments that address the underlying disease rather than simply manage symptoms.

He said its research programme focused on changing the course of mCALR-driven ET and MF.

Prosek described the acquisition as an opportunity to accelerate the programme’s development under Lilly.

He also acknowledged the contributions of the company’s employees, scientific advisers and investors in advancing the candidate towards clinical development.

Lilly expands oncology dealmaking

Founded in 2025 by J.P. Morgan Life Sciences Private Capital, the life sciences investment division of J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Calytrix Bio is based in Wellesley Hills, Massachusetts.

The acquisition adds to Lilly’s recent business development activity in biotechnology.

Last month, the pharmaceutical company expanded its partnership and licensing agreement with California-based Gate Bioscience to develop molecular gate therapies for proteins that have been difficult to target with conventional drug development approaches.

The Calytrix transaction also reflects the pharmaceutical industry’s continued interest in acquiring early-stage biotechnology programmes with potential to address genetically defined diseases.

For large drugmakers, such deals provide access to specialised research platforms and investigational therapies while allowing milestone-based payments to link acquisition costs to development progress.
